clues: This port town sits on the slopes of Mount Carmel by the sea. It lies on a wide bay on the coast of a small land in the far east.
Frost is rare here, and snow is more rare still. The last snow fell in 1950, and cold snaps come in the early hours of the day.
Long ago, in the years near 300, this town was known far and wide for its dye works. That craft set it apart in its age.
The town has a small train line that runs deep under the ground. For years it was the sole such line in the whole land.
The world seat of the Baháʼí faith stands in this town. Folk come from all lands to pray at this holy site.
